summary: Calistoga sits at the very top of the Napa Valley, wedged against the base of Mount Saint Helena, which means the town is literally where the valley dead-ends into forested volcanic slopes — and that geography defines everything about living here. At just 2.6 square miles and roughly 5,200 people, the entire town is compact enough to walk end to end, with a small-grid downtown of tasting rooms, restaurants, and hot-spring spas that reflect an economy built almost entirely on wine, tourism, and hospitality. That economic narrowness is the central tension: the median home value of $702,700 against a median household income of around $84,900 produces a price-to-income ratio above 8, which places ownership firmly out of reach for most locally employed households earning at or below the median. Rents averaging $1,798 a month are more manageable but still consume a significant share of that income. The payoff is tangible — 9.3 hours of daily sunshine, warm dry summers averaging 70°F highs, and direct access to Robert Louis Stevenson State Park and the Palisades trail system right at the edge of town. Commuting south to the city of Napa takes roughly 30 minutes on a good day along the two-lane Silverado Trail, and job-switching without leaving town is constrained by the narrow employer base. Calistoga is a place where the physical beauty and small-town walkability are real, but the gap between what the local economy pays and what housing costs is equally real.
